data: France's first satellite, Astérix, launched on a Diamant A in 1965

Facts from the Wikipedia articles on Hammaguir (English and French), Astérix, Diamant and the SpaceNews account of the 26 November 1965 launch. The pad position is the Diamant launch pad coordinates given on English Wikipedia. The range belonged to the French Army's CIEES; the Diamant programme was CNES's.
Nov. 26, 1965: France begins launch legacy of Diamant — SpaceNews

Hammaguir was a French rocket range in the Algerian Sahara, about 120 km south-west of Béchar. The French Army's CIEES developed it from the late 1940s for sounding rockets and missiles. Its Brigitte complex tested the 'precious stones' rockets (Agate, Topaze, Émeraude, Saphir, Rubis), which led to the Diamant launcher. On 26 November 1965 a Diamant A put Astérix, France's first satellite, into orbit: France became the third country to orbit a satellite on its own rocket, after the Soviet Union and the United States. Three more French satellites followed in 1966 and 1967. Under the Évian accords France kept the base until July 1967, and Diamant launches then moved to Kourou in French Guiana. More than 270 rockets were fired from Hammaguir.
